script.analysis: All 19,258 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: your $41,000 savings vs coworker Grace's ~$300,000 on the same $52,000 salary over 10 years, attributed to one 20-minute decision; like CTA. Inflation erosion ($1 in 2000 -> ~51 cents), HYSA ~4% vs inflation ~4%, asset composition by wealth group (bottom half home/car; top 1% ~2% cash; top 10% own ~90% of stocks), honest surplus caveat flagged early. Step 1 emergency-fund "line" and automatic overflow; Step 2 order (match, toxic debt, tax-advantaged, HSA); Step 3 automation (64% opt-in vs 94% auto-enroll participation) and behavior gap; Step 4 index fund, 1% fee example, active underperformance; buy-borrow aside; compounding table for $500/month; start-at-25 vs 35; surplus caveat (59% can't cover $1,000); late "faceless YouTube" community CTA (claims 10+ successful channels), disclaimer, close. Clear stepwise structure with a framing story, but the central Grace result and several figures are inconsistent. ASR not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:9700 Grace vs Greg: if Greg accumulated ~$41,000 of savings over 10 years (~$4,100/year), investing the same deposits at 10% would reach only ~$65,000; reaching ~$300,000 in 10 years requires ~$18,800/year (~36% of a $52,000 salary) even at 10%. The "$260,000 cost" of not investing is therefore not supported by "same habit of putting money aside". $1 in 2000 buying ~51 cents today is roughly consistent with CPI. "Inflation around 4%" in July 2026 not verified and likely above recent CPI prints; HYSA ~4% plausible.

0:9700 Top 10% owning ~90% of US stocks consistent with Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts (~93%). Top 1% holding ~2% in cash unverified. Opt-in ~64% vs auto-enroll ~94% participation consistent with Vanguard How America Saves. HSA triple tax advantage correct federally.

9700:19258 $500/month at 7%: 10y ~$86,500, 20y ~$260,500, 30y ~$610,000, 40y ~$1.31M - all consistent. But start at 25 vs 35 to 65 at 7% gives ~$1.31M vs ~$610,000, not "$1.37M vs $740,000" - the $740K contradicts the script's own 30-year figure; the ~$700K gap and $60K skipped deposits are approximately right. 1% fee on $10,000 over 30 years costs ~$18,700 at 7% (vs 6%), ~$41,800 at 10% (vs 9%); "around $40,000" requires ~10% returns, inconsistent with the 7% real return used later. Active-manager underperformance and investor behavior gap correctly characterized in general terms.

9700:19258 Borrowing against assets presented as a rich-person gear without leverage/margin-call risk caveats. 59% unable to cover a $1,000 expense from savings consistent with Bankrate 2025 survey. Community CTA claim of "more than 10 successful channels" is a self-claim, unverified.
